Personal experiences? Thoughts? Suggestions? I'm going to have a receiver or two to coat soon and was wondering what people have used/thought.
Cerakote C or the over cure vs Alumahyde vs Duracoat etc...
Never used. Sorry. Always kept my guns in their original form. It looks like it might be worth while.

I've done Cerakote, the kind you send in to a company. It's super nice. Very even and tough. I baby my guns so I'm probably not the best to person to ask about durability but it stands up perfectly fine to normal shooting. Others have really put theirs through the paces and it holds up fine for them as well. You can find them all over the web on various gun forums. I decided on the one you send in to a company because it's usually super affordable anyway and I know it will get done right and nice and even. I've never have really good luck painting shit and getting it even.

What I REALLY love is Robars NP3 coating. Teflon embedded nickle stuff. Slick enough you can fire it with no oil. Not that you would but you could if you wanted. Heard stories of side by side tests with NP3 BCGs and the uncoated ones eventually getting gunked up and not firing and the NP3's going fine. Super easy to clean because it's so slick. Holds up super well to stuff like salt water. The NP3+ coating is even better on the chemical/salt water characteristics by an order of magnitude or so. The downside is only 1 color (but I like it, a slightly brownish chrome I guess), its pretty expensive and turnaround time can be up to 2 months. Because it's so expensive I only have certain parts coated. Both my pistol slides are coated, gives a super sexy 2 tone look, super easy to clean the breach face, and has a ton of surfaces that you normally would lube up anyways so I don't have to worry if I miss oiling some part on accident. The next thing I'm sending in is my ARs BCG when I can afford it.
